condition: sports head collision with 2 minute blackout and persistent forehead headache
level_rationale: A 2-minute loss of consciousness immediately following a basketball head-to-head collision 2 hours ago with an ongoing forehead headache meets high-risk acute head-injury criteria requiring immediate Emergency Department neuroimaging and neurological evaluation, whereas feeling briefly lightheaded for 5 seconds on the court after the same head bump with a mild dull forehead headache 2 hours later warrants an outpatient clinic sports head-injury assessment before returning to play rather than emergency care or unassessed self-care.

everyday_sources.adaptation: Past-tense verbal form 'blacked out' corresponding to noun 'blackout' ('A temporary loss of consciousness'), matching core entry 'blackout / blacked out' in dialect_lexicon_20261109.json in the acute head-trauma unconsciousness sense with zero alcohol context.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Core dialect lexicon swap ('lost consciousness' vs 'blacked out', retained in everyday_paraphrase) + single-fact post-impact neurological severity and duration de-escalation control (-cf, L4 to L2).

design_note: Uses four strictly atomic facts (age 20, basketball head collision 2 hours ago, 2-minute loss of consciousness on the court, and mild dull forehead headache now) with no banned diagnosis label ('concussion' omitted from all texts) and no second emergent red flag stranded in f1, f2, or f4. Changing only fact f3 from 'blacked out for 2 minutes' to 'felt briefly lightheaded for 5 seconds' stays inside the exact sports head-impact case and shifts care cleanly from Emergency Department neuroimaging (level 4) to outpatient physician head-injury clearance (level 2) with zero stated negatives under Rules A and D.
